The '''Elin Roe system''' was situated in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]]<ref name="TEA" /> and contained the terrestrial celestial body [[Elin Roe]] as well as its [[Moon/Legends|moons]], of which there were at least five.<ref name="CRO" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Interceptor (Guardian-class light cruiser)|''Interceptor'']], a [[Guardian-class light cruiser|''Guardian''-class light cruiser]] of the [[Imperial Office of Customs/Legends|Imperial Office of Customs]] under the [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Hallyn Phlynne]], performed spot checks on [[Starship/Legends|starships]] traveling through the [[Star system/Legends|star system]].<ref name="Journal2">{{JournalCite|2|Smuggler's Log}}</ref>

At some point by the [[Time/Legends|time]] shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], during a pursuit of a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] target on Elin Roe, [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] team known as the [[Yagaran Four]] activated the dangerously modified [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] of their [[Unidentified YT-1300 light freighter|YT-1300 light freighter]]. The [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|starship]] then exploded, [[Death/Legends|killing]] the Yagaran Four and emitting a [[Cloud/Legends|cloud]] of [[Radiation/Legends|radioactive]] dust that washed over [[Elin Roe's fifth moon]].<ref name="CRO" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Elin Roe system was introduced in an installment of the '"[[Smuggler's Log]]" series of [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] source articles that was authored by [[Peter M. Schweighofer|Peter Schweighofer]] for use with ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' and published in the [[May]] [[1994]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 2|second issue]] of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine.<ref name="Journal2" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the system in grid square N-12.<ref name="TEA" />
